note: First end-to-end three-arm runs with the planner driving a real cooling array as a second powered die. skylake 7-core, 10 nm trace, 2000 um tile pitch, 200 um burial, 88 CFM. SMOKE TESTS: reduced iteration limits (--mr-iter 2-3, --max-iter 12-20) to prove the wiring, NOT production settings. 25 Aug 2026.

arms.array_idle: 30 um GaAs pixel array, 0 W of light

low_density.reading: 10.2 K of passive gain before any light; the laser correctly does nothing because no block is above target. That the laser term is exactly zero here is the point -- a two-arm comparison would have reported the whole 10.2 K as an MR result.

high_density.reading: The UNPOWERED array alone rescues a die that has no steady state under grease. Swapping 30 um of TIM for 30 um of GaAs is sufficient on its own; the laser then adds 4.9 K and +11.8% throughput for 2.76 W removed. Under the old two-arm scheme this would have been reported as 'MR rescues a runaway die', crediting the light with what the material substitution achieved. That is precisely the confound the three arms exist to remove, and it fired on the first real run.

wiring_verified: every row stamps placement='array_above', n_tiles=12, pitch and the stack spec; control stamps placement='none' and 0 tiles
bugs_the_guards_caught: spec string set mr_layer but not mr_powered, so the array rendered as an inert slab with no tile floorplan -- caught by session_powers()'s 'array would silently remove nothing' check
driver converted plan->stack sign a second time after CoolingApplication had already done it, flipping removal into heating -- caught by fill_mr_flp_template()'s sign guard
